title: They begged for the chance, then walked away when it came.
subtitle: Big promises made before the test arrives
then: Mujahid said the prophet here was Samuel. Wahb says the Children of Israel had {trap}lost their land, their children, and the Ark{/trap}. They demanded a king to lead them. Their prophet asked: would you hold back if it were prescribed? They swore not. When it came, {trap}most turned away{/trap}.
now: If I just had the time, I would memorize Qur'an. If I just had the money, I would give. Then the free weekend comes, the bonus arrives. {trap}The promise evaporates.{/trap} Allah knows the gap between what we say and what we do.
old: If the right situation came, I would definitely step up.
new: The test is not what I promise beforehand, but what I do when the moment arrives.
try: Pick one thing you keep saying you would do if only. Do a small part of it today.

title: Allah chose the poor water-carrier. Knowledge and strength over status.
subtitle: When we judge who deserves to lead
then: Ibn Kathir says Talut was {trap}not from the royal house of Judah, and was poor{/trap}; some said he carried water, others that he dyed leather. The people argued with their prophet instead of accepting. He replied: {reward}Allah chose him and increased him in knowledge and stature{/reward}. Allah gives authority to whom He wills.
now: The new manager came from the warehouse floor, not the right university. The imam is young and from the wrong family. {trap}You catch yourself sneering.{/trap} The verse asks: is your objection about ability, or about pride?
old: Leaders should come from the right background and the right money.
new: Allah raises people by knowledge and strength, and my pride is no judge of who deserves it.
try: Say one sincere word of support to someone in a role you secretly thought you deserved more.

title: The sign came with sakinah: calm sent down from your Lord.
subtitle: What returned to them with the Ark
then: Their prophet promised the {reward}Ark taken by their enemy would come back{/reward}. Qatadah and Ar-Rabi said the sakinah in it meant grace and mercy. Ibn Abbas said it held {reward}Moses' staff and remnants of the Tablets{/reward}, and that angels carried it until they placed it before Talut while people watched.
now: Before the job interview, the surgery, the hard conversation, you want a guarantee. What you need first is a settled heart. {reward}Sakinah is the gift that comes before victory.{/reward} Ask for it by name.
old: I will feel calm once everything works out.
new: Calm is something Allah sends down, and I can ask Him for it before anything works out.
try: Before your next stressful moment, ask Allah: send down sakinah on my heart.

title: A handful from the river, or drink your fill and fall away.
subtitle: Small restraints sort out who is ready
then: Talut's army met a river. Ibn Abbas said: {reward}whoever took a handful was quenched; whoever drank freely stayed thirsty{/reward}. Al-Bara said the Companions at Badr were about the same number as those who crossed with Talut, a little over three hundred. Facing Goliath, the certain ones said: {idea}how often has a small group overcome a large one{/idea}.
now: The snack drawer. The extra hour of scrolling. One more episode. {trap}Drinking your fill never quite satisfies.{/trap} A handful is enough, and the small restraints build the person who can face the big tests.
old: Small indulgences do not matter when the big test comes.
new: The way I handle a small thirst trains me for the big battle.
try: Pick one craving today and stop at a handful.

title: Pour patience on us, plant our feet, give us victory.
subtitle: The dua of the few before the giant
then: When the few under Talut faced the many under Goliath, they did not boast. Ibn Kathir says they asked Allah to {reward}send down patience from Him{/reward}, to {reward}keep their feet firm and save them from running away and feebleness{/reward}, and to grant victory.
now: The exam hall. The courtroom. Facing a boss twice your size in the company. {idea}You do not have to manufacture courage.{/idea} You can ask for it to be poured on you like water.
old: I have to find the strength in myself to face this.
new: Patience and steady feet are gifts I can ask Allah to pour on me.
try: Memorize this dua today: Rabbana afrigh alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana.

title: A young soldier, David, felled the giant by Allah's permission.
subtitle: How Allah keeps the earth from ruin

row.title: the strong do as they like

then: Ibn Kathir notes Israelite reports that {idea}David killed Goliath with a sling{/idea}. Allah then gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him what He willed. If Allah did not {idea}push back some people by means of others{/idea}, the earth would be corrupted; Ibn Kathir links this to 22:40, where houses of worship would be torn down.
now: The bully in the office who no one stands up to. The neighbor who intimidates the street. {idea}Allah often stops harm through ordinary people who step in.{/idea} Sometimes that person is you.
old: Someone else will deal with the injustice around me.
new: Allah protects the earth through people who stand up, and I might be one of them.
try: Step in kindly for one person being treated unfairly today, even in a small way.

title: These stories are told to you in truth. You are a messenger.
subtitle: Why old stories land on the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir says these verses tell the story {idea}exactly as it happened{/idea}, matching what remained in the earlier scriptures. Then Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ directly: {reward}you are one of the messengers{/reward}. The small band in Madinah heard their own situation in the few who crossed the river.
now: You read about Talut and think it is a children's story. But you are the one facing a giant at work, at home, in your own habits. {idea}It is told to you in truth, for you.{/idea}
old: Quran stories are history lessons about other people.
new: These stories are true and told to me, for the giants I face today.
try: Retell the Talut story to a child or friend tonight in your own words.

title: Allah ranked the messengers. Do not turn them into a fight.
subtitle: Honor all the prophets without point-scoring
then: Ibn Kathir reports a Muslim who {trap}slapped a Jewish man in an argument over Moses' rank{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}do not prefer me over the prophets{/idea}, and spoke of seeing Moses holding the Throne on the Day. Ranking belongs to Allah, not to our quarrels. Later generations still fought after clear proofs, by Allah's will.
now: The comment thread where someone insults another faith's prophet, and you want to hit back harder. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ himself told us not to turn the prophets into a contest.{/idea} Respect them all, and let Allah rank them.
old: Defending my faith means proving my prophet is the best in every argument.
new: I honor every messenger Allah sent, and leave their ranking to Him.
try: Read about one prophet you know little about today, with respect.
